recentItems.title: PARTISANS DEVASTATE RUSSIA'S REAR: large-scale Operation ‘Barrel’ blocks enemy supply trains
recentItems.description:
Ukrainian Defense Forces successfully struck the Russian cargo ship Aroyat, dealing another blow to the occupiers' maritime logistics in the Black Sea. Concurrently, the partisan movement Freedom of Russia carried out Operation "Barrel," causing $10 million in damages to the Russian oil sector and blocking key rail routes. In response to systematic strikes by the Armed Forces of Ukraine, Putin signed a decree classifying data on the energy crisis while preparing a new wave of forced mobilization. On the front lines, operators of the Unmanned Systems Forces destroy the equivalent of an enemy battalion every day, while the 3rd Army Corps successfully continues Operation "Vivaldi" near Lyman. Facing colossal losses that outpace recruitment rates, the Kremlin has been forced to involve over 18,000 troops from North Korea.

recentItems.title: Russia CAUSES GENOCIDE – HORRIFIC humanitarian catastrophe in OLESHKY
recentItems.description:
The town of Oleshky in Southern Ukraine. Occupied territory. The settlement, where thousands of people remain, is virtually under a blockade: roads are mined, drones fly constantly, and civilians live under the threat of shelling and attacks by the occupiers.

In Oleshky, electricity, water, gas, communications, fuel, food, and medical aid are almost non-existent, and due to a lack of generator fuel, the hospital cannot perform complex surgeries. Because of mined roads and relentless attacks, aid barely arrives, people suffer from hunger, and Russian occupiers even seize humanitarian food supplies and target those who receive them.

Witnesses describe Oleshky as a place where people have lost all sense of safety and dignity, yet still hold on to the hope of returning home.

recentItems.title: Zelenskyy confirms Putin plans to spend $12 BILLION on DRONES and ATTACK Ukraine's ENERGY GRID
recentItems.description:
The Kremlin is still not ready to end the war — this is confirmed by both President Zelenskyy and the Chairman of the Bundestag Foreign Affairs Committee, Johann Wadephul, following his meeting with Lavrov. Putin is searching for new excuses to continue his aggression, accusing Ukraine of striking civilian infrastructure "first," even though Russia started doing so back in 2022. Moscow rejects an energy truce and is ramping up drone production for 2027, planning to spend $12 billion on jet-powered Shaheds alone. ISW analysts believe Putin is betting on terrorist strikes against Ukraine's energy grid this winter. For the Kremlin, the war has become a core element of domestic politics, without which it would be difficult to justify restrictions and costs to its citizens.

recentItems.title: KREMLIN’S MISCALCULATION: Putin loses his army and targets civilians out of panic!
recentItems.description:
Warriors of the 3rd Separate Assault Brigade achieved major success during Operation Vivaldi, liberating a number of settlements from the occupiers in the Lyman direction. Through unique innovations — including BTR-60 armored personnel carriers repurposed into robotic kamikazes and ground platforms deployed via heavy drones — the Armed Forces of Ukraine breached the enemy’s formidable defenses and destroyed their fortifications. In total, Ukrainian forces reclaimed control over 51 square kilometers of territory, inflicting heavy casualties and material losses on Russian troops. Alongside frontline combat, reconnaissance units continue to destroy critical military infrastructure, logistics, and communications deep within enemy-held territories. Military experts note that the mass deployment of uncrewed ground and aerial systems is fundamentally reshaping modern battlefield tactics while effectively safeguarding the lives of Ukrainian defenders.

recentItems.title: Zelenskyy confirms INTERCEPTION of ballistic missiles. NATO & EU prepare SPECIAL TRIBUNAIL for Putin
recentItems.description:
The enemy launched another massive attack on peaceful Ukrainian cities, deploying ballistic missiles and over a hundred drones across nine regions. Air defense forces shot down 109 aerial targets, including Zircon and Iskander missiles, while President Zelenskyy expressed gratitude to international partners for the provided weaponry. Meanwhile, during its autumn session, the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe called for increased pressure on Russia and the accelerated creation of a special tribunal. NATO and the EU emphasized that the Kremlin's hybrid attacks and sabotage in Europe will only strengthen the allies' resolve to provide military assistance to Ukraine. Against the backdrop of intense frontline fighting, diplomatic discussions continue regarding further steps to secure the region and leverage frozen Russian assets.

Meanwhile, Kyiv faced another hostile drone attack, resulting in damage to residential buildings and civilian infrastructure. On the front line, fighters of the 3rd Army Corps of the Armed Forces of Ukraine successfully deployed ground combat robots during Operation "Vivaldi," liberating around 40 square kilometers of territory. In Brussels and European capitals, concern is growing over Russian sabotage, attempted arson at defense plants, and satellite provocations in Poland and Germany.
